_comment: The Librarian's map. Tiered by what kind of question you have. 'access' flags paywalls, memberships and feeds that block automated pulls. Edit freely; the Librarian reads this file.

sections.question: What does the law or regulator actually say? (US)

entries.name: Federal Register
entries.why: every proposed and final rule, executive order and notice; the controlling text

entries.name: FERC eLibrary and orders
entries.why: approves and directs NERC CIP standards; orders are the primary record

entries.name: NERC Reliability Standards (CIP-002 to CIP-015)
entries.why: the mandatory bulk-power-system cyber standards, with effective dates
entries.access: free; news page has no RSS

entries.name: TSA pipeline security directives
entries.why: the oil and gas pipeline cyber regime; check each directive's version and expiry

entries.name: congress.gov
entries.why: statutes and bills, e.g. the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015 sunset and any NDAA extension

entries.name: DOE CESER
entries.why: the energy sector risk management agency; programs, leadership, reports

entries.name: NRC cybersecurity (10 CFR 73.54)
entries.why: nuclear plant cyber rule and inspections

sections.question: Is this vulnerability real and is it exploited?

entries.name: CISA ICS advisories
entries.why: the authoritative US advisory per ICS product, several per week, some tagged 'Used in Energy'
entries.access: free; RSS returns 403 to many automated clients, read the site

entries.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
entries.why: if a CVE is here, exploitation is confirmed by the US government

entries.name: NVD
entries.why: CVE record, CVSS, references

entries.name: Vendor PSIRT/ProductCERT pages
entries.why: Siemens, Schneider, Rockwell, ABB, Honeywell, Zyxel each publish their own advisories; the vendor advisory outranks any outlet

sections.question: Who is the actor and what is the tradecraft?
sections.tier: vendor research (attribute by name, flag as seller)

entries.name: Dragos (Year in Review, threat group pages)
entries.why: deepest public ICS threat-group tracking
entries.access: free with email gate; no working RSS

entries.name: Mandiant / Google Threat Intelligence
entries.why: nation-state attributions, Sandworm and Volt Typhoon reporting

entries.name: Microsoft Threat Intelligence
entries.why: Volt Typhoon and similar campaigns; large telemetry

entries.name: Claroty Team82, Nozomi Labs, Forescout Vedere
entries.why: OT vulnerability research

entries.name: MITRE ATT&CK for ICS
entries.why: the shared vocabulary for techniques; use it to compare incidents

sections.question: What is the research and academic view?

entries.name: IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid
entries.why: grid cyber-physical security research
entries.access: paywalled; many preprints on arXiv eess.SY / cs.CR

entries.name: International Journal of Critical Infrastructure Protection (Elsevier)
entries.why: the dedicated CIP journal

entries.name: Journal of Cybersecurity (Oxford)
entries.why: policy and interdisciplinary cyber research

entries.name: Computers & Security (Elsevier)
entries.why: ICS intrusion detection and OT security papers

entries.name: arXiv cs.CR and eess.SY
entries.why: free preprints, including grid and ICS security

entries.name: NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3
entries.why: the free OT security guide; the substitute for ISA/IEC 62443

entries.name: ISA/IEC 62443
entries.why: the OT security standard family

entries.name: SANS ICS resources and the SANS ICS Summit
entries.why: practitioner whitepapers and incident reviews

entries.name: Lawfare, Just Security, CSIS, Atlantic Council Cyber Statecraft
entries.why: policy analysis of energy cyber law and geopolitics

entries.name: Scite / Google Scholar
entries.why: find and check citations; Scite shows whether later papers support or contrast a claim

entries.name: Stanford Cyber Policy Center and Internet Observatory
entries.why: policy research on critical infrastructure, platform and state cyber behaviour; feeds malformed, read by hand

entries.name: UC Berkeley Center for Long-Term Cybersecurity
entries.why: futures and policy research; read automatically via feed

entries.name: MIT Technology Review
entries.why: AI and energy reporting, data-centre power; read automatically via feed

entries.name: Stanford HAI AI Index
entries.why: annual data on AI compute, cost and energy for the Technologist

entries.name: The Record, CyberScoop, SecurityWeek, Dark Reading, BleepingComputer, Krebs
entries.why: the allowlisted feeds; fast, US-centric, vendor-adjacent to varying degrees

entries.name: Utility Dive, E&E News, S&P Global Commodity Insights
entries.why: energy-industry framing of the same events
entries.access: Utility Dive blocks automated pulls (403); E&E and S&P paywalled

entries.name: Industrial Cyber
entries.why: OT-only trade press, relays regulator and vendor notices

entries.name: E-ISAC
entries.why: the electricity sector's sharing body; the richest incident data
entries.access: members only; public output via NERC alerts

entries.name: ONG-ISAC, DNG-ISAC
entries.why: oil and gas, downstream gas sharing

entries.name: NERC Lessons Learned and GADS/TADS
entries.why: post-event reports, some cyber-related

entries.name: DOE OE-417 electric disturbance reports
entries.why: mandatory US outage and disturbance filings, including cyber events

entries.name: CISA ICS-CERT historical advisories and the ICS Advisory Project
entries.why: dashboards over all ICS advisories by sector and vendor

sections.question: Magazines, long-form and commentary (context, not confirmation)

entries.name: WIRED Security
entries.why: narrative investigations (Sandworm, Colonial); read automatically via feed

entries.name: Schneier on Security
entries.why: policy and technical commentary; read automatically via feed

entries.name: Lawfare
entries.why: legal analysis of cyber and critical infrastructure; feed blocks automation, read by hand

entries.name: Dark Reading / SecurityWeek features
entries.why: vendor-sponsored analysis; already in the allowlist

sections.question: Forums and communities (never a source; sometimes a subject)

entries.name: SANS ICS community and ICS Summit talks
entries.why: practitioner discussion; cite the published paper or talk, not the thread

entries.name: Reddit r/ICS, r/netsec; Mastodon infosec
entries.why: early signals and rumours; a story's origin, never its confirmation

entries.name: Ransomware leak sites, Telegram channels
entries.why: attacker claims; counted as claims in the record, never as confirmed

sections.question: Incident datasets and case registers (discovery, then verify at the primary)
sections.tier: curated databases: discovery aids, not final authority

entries.name: EuRepoC (European Repository of Cyber Incidents)
entries.why: expert-reviewed dataset; 175 energy-tagged rows in v1.3, most without coded initial access; triangulate, do not cite as final

entries.name: The Observatory (energy cyber incidents)
entries.why: has duplicate campaign rows and some wrong sector/attribution fields per the report; discovery only

entries.name: SektorCERT (Denmark)
entries.why: the Danish 2023 Zyxel campaign report; model for counting a campaign once

entries.name: CERT Polska incident reports
entries.why: Poland December 2025 distributed-energy campaign and follow-up; already an allowlisted feed

entries.name: MITRE ATT&CK for ICS case studies and software pages
entries.why: technical reconstructions (Ukraine 2016, Industroyer, Stuxnet) with evidence limits stated

entries.name: DOE C2M2
entries.why: governance model for the defensive program

entries.name: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada findings (Nova Scotia Power)
entries.why: an unusually detailed official incident reconstruction

sections.question: Sector threat reports (annual or periodic; vendor and government)
sections.tier: reports: context and numbers to verify, not incident evidence

entries.name: Industrial Cyber: resilience report on energy and utilities (ransomware, vulnerable OT)
entries.why: trade-press summary of a vendor resilience report; page returns 403 to automated fetch, read by hand; find the underlying report and cite that

entries.name: Cybersecurity Dive: the hacking campaign against US water systems (2026-08-20)
entries.why: well-sourced running account: 12+ states, Minnesota 30+ systems on July 26-27, Rockwell Logix (CVE-2021-22681), Schneider M340, Siemens S7-1200; Iran-linked suspected, APT Iran/CyberAv3ngers claim unverified; CISA/FBI July warning covers water AND energy

entries.name: NJCCIC Energy Sector Threat Analysis Report
entries.why: state government (New Jersey) sector analysis; page returns 403 to automated fetch; read by hand

entries.name: SecurityScorecard: Energy Sector Cybersecurity Report (third-party risk)
entries.why: vendor research; headline '90% of the largest energy companies had a third-party breach in 12 months' with no sample or method on the page; gated; a ratings vendor selling the fix

entries.name: IBM X-Force Threat Intelligence Index 2026
entries.why: vendor annual: public-facing exploitation +44% YoY, 56% of disclosed flaws need no auth, ransomware groups +49%; no energy share stated on the page; method not described; gated

entries.name: Reuters: energy firms face AI-enhanced cyber attacks amid connectivity push (REEII, 2026-09-01)
entries.why: wire report from the Reuters Energy Innovation event; Reuters blocks automated fetch so the content is unread here; cite only after reading

entries.name: Railroad Commission of Texas cyber warning (GovTech, 2026-11-02)
entries.why: state regulator warning to oil and gas on cyber threats citing attacks involving energy tankers bound for Texas; from the pasted daily brief; find the RRC primary notice

entries.name: CISA ICSA-26-307-01: Subnet Solutions PowerSYSTEM Center
entries.why: CVE-2026-63017 and CVE-2026-63774, CVSS 9.0; energy-sector OT software; also relayed by INCIBE-CERT in our bundle

entries.name: CERT-UA: UAC-0050 campaign impersonating DTEK (2026-10-29)
entries.why: energy-themed phishing against Ukrainian government; impersonation, not a DTEK compromise
entries.access: free; CERT-UA is an allowlisted feed
